draft.title: Green bans
card: A green ban was a refusal by workers to build on a site because the project would harm the environment or heritage. It began in Sydney in the early 1970s.
The bans were put in place by the New South Wales Builders Labourers' Federation, a union of building workers. Its members chose to refuse work, so the developer could not build.

Residents asked the union for help. One of the first bans protected Kelly's Bush, an area of bushland on the Sydney Harbour shore, from being cleared for houses. Later bans helped save historic buildings and neighbourhoods such as The Rocks.
Green bans were unusual because workers and residents joined forces. Workers used their power over building work to protect places, not to win better pay.
draft.remember: Green bans: builders refused to work on projects that would destroy bushland or heritage, helped by residents.

a.q: What was a green ban in 1970s Sydney?
opts: Builders refusing to work on a site that harmed the environment
A law that stopped developers from clearing any bushland
A protest by residents who blocked a site with their bodies
A union strike to win higher pay for building workers
a.why: A green ban was a refusal by building workers to take on a project that would harm bushland or heritage. A strike for higher pay is the tempting wrong answer, because the workers were acting to protect places and not to win better pay.
a.clue: Think about who stopped the work and why.

b.q: Residents of a Sydney suburb in 1972 feared a developer would clear their local bushland. Why could a green ban stop the project?
opts: Builders agreed not to work on it, so it could not go ahead
The government passed a law that cancelled the project
The developer was fined by the residents' action group
Builders were paid more to leave the site alone
b.why: A green ban worked because the building workers themselves refused to do the work, so the developer could not build. It was not a law or a fine, because the unions acted by their own choice. The residents asked for help but did not stop the work themselves.
b.clue: Who would have had to do the building?
